tagline: The thousand-year capital of the Silla Kingdom is a 'museum without walls', full of royal burial mounds, stone pagodas, Bulguksa Temple and the Seokguram Buddha.
overview: Gyeongju was the capital of the Silla Kingdom for nearly 1,000 years, from 57 BC to AD 935, and much of that past is still in plain sight. Grassy royal tombs rise in the middle of town, and the Gyeongju Historic Areas are listed by UNESCO.

Tumuli Park holds the Cheonmachong tomb, which can be entered, and Cheomseongdae, one of the oldest surviving astronomical observatories in East Asia, stands nearby. Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond are especially beautiful when lit up at night, and the Gyeongju National Museum displays gold crowns and the giant Emille Bell.

On Tohamsan mountain, Bulguksa Temple and the Seokguram Grotto, with its granite Buddha looking out to sea, are joint UNESCO sites. Cherry blossoms around Bomun Lake, the Gyochon hanok village and Hwangnidan-gil's cafés make the city a popular weekend escape.

funFacts.title: A 1,000-YEAR CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Gyeongju was Silla's capital for about 992 years.

funFacts.title: MUSEUM WITHOUT WALLS
funFacts.text: The city has so many historic sites that it is called a museum without walls.

funFacts.title: AN ANCIENT OBSERVATORY
funFacts.text: Cheomseongdae, from the 7th century, is one of East Asia's oldest observatories.

funFacts.title: GOLD CROWNS
funFacts.text: Silla tombs yielded spectacular gold crowns now in the national museum.

funFacts.title: TWO UNESCO LISTINGS
funFacts.text: Bulguksa/Seokguram and the Gyeongju Historic Areas are both World Heritage Sites.

funFacts.title: A GIANT BELL
funFacts.text: The Divine Bell of King Seongdeok weighs about 19 tonnes.

funFacts.title: TOMBS IN TOWN
funFacts.text: Large grassy royal burial mounds stand right in the city centre.

funFacts.title: GYEONGJU BREAD
funFacts.text: Hwangnam-ppang, a red-bean pastry, is the local treat.

funFacts.title: APEC HOST

funFacts.title: CHERRY BLOSSOM CITY
